title: The same bioelectric trigger is reinterpreted by context (monensin: tails vs legs)

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The same bioelectric trigger is reinterpreted by context (monensin: tails vs legs)

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Low-information bioelectric triggers are interpreted by competent tissues according to context: the voltage-modifying reagent monensin induces tail regrowth in tadpoles but leg regrowth in froglets, never the reverse, preserving high-level information such as 'build whatever normally goes at this location'.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Here, the same bioelectric stimulus is functionally reinterpreted based on the specific context, preserving salient, high-level information like “build whatever normally goes at this location” (in the case of the appendage regeneration trigger).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere”. Scope: Xenopus tadpole tail and froglet hindlimb regeneration

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The anatomical readout and contrasting outcomes are direct. Published measurements can probably check the reported cases, but data adequacy is limited by separate protocols and uncertain access to raw images and counts.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare appendage identity and regeneration frequency after matched systemic monensin treatment at tadpole tail wounds and froglet leg wounds. Tails only at tail sites and legs only at limb sites support context dependence; swapped or context-independent structures refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw individual-level regeneration data may not be deposited.

Developmental stage, dose and wound type differ between experiments.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The anatomical contrast is straightforward to score, and published tail experiments already report regeneration indices after a brief monensin treatment. Those numbers, and the corresponding leg results, are not a public dataset an outside group can reanalyze, and they have not been compiled from independent replications. Resolving the location-specific claim needs the paired wound-site data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply the same monensin regimen to tadpole tail amputations and froglet hindlimb amputations and score the identity of the regenerate. Site-appropriate structures, and no tail-from-leg or leg-from-tail outcomes, would support the claim; swapped or nonspecific structures would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The froglet leg series is not an independent public replication with raw counts.

Monensin also changes sodium, pH, and cell stress, so structure identity has to be scored, not merely whether anything regrows.

Tail regeneration indices are published from one group and are not a deposited animal-level table.
